navCards.about: My musical journey from Havana to the world stage

about.title: Passion Meets Precision
about.p1: I am **Aniel Someillan**, a versatile musician hailing from the vibrant streets of Havana, Cuba. My journey with music began at a young age, fueled by the rich cultural tapestry of my homeland. This passion led me to pursue a formal education, eventually obtaining a **Bachelor's in Classical Guitar and Arts**.
about.p2: However, my musical exploration didn't stop there. Over time, I transitioned into a professional **Electric and Double Bass player**, instruments that allowed me to find the rhythmic heartbeat of jazz and contemporary music.
about.p3: One of my most significant achievements was winning the prestigious **Jazz Junior Competition** with my project "Ilú." This recognition was a turning point, showcasing my commitment to pushing the boundaries of traditional sounds. My dedication to the craft further earned me a coveted invitation to the **Montreux Jazz Academy**, where I had the privilege of learning from and performing with some of the world's greatest musical minds.
about.quote: "Life without playing music is inconceivable to me."
about.p4: Whether I am performing on international stages or recording in the studio, my goal remains the same: to create music that resonates deeply and carries the listener away. I continue to explore new sounds and collaborations, always keeping the spirit of Havana in my strings.

s2.label: The Beginning
s2.body: A Cuban musician. Eight years in Brazil. An imaginary city that repeats, night after night, in his dreams — built from streets of Havana and buildings of São Paulo.

s3.label: The Dream
s3.body: At the same time he was reading Machado de Assis — his dead narrator, his impossible irony, his city between two worlds.

s4.label: The Sound
s4.announcer: AND THE SOUND? LADIES AND GENTLEMEN...
s4.body: A mostly vocal album. Three languages: español · português · english. Lyrics about society, love and pain — with an enormous, deliberate sarcastic touch.

s5.label: The Studio
s5.studioLabel: THE PERSONAL STUDIO OF SILVIO RODRÍGUEZ
s5.body: Four tracks already recorded. The album travels to São Paulo — then returns to Havana to close where it began.

s6.label: The Cast
s6.threadBody: Dagoberto González comes from Orquesta Aragón — the same orchestra that popularised Tres Estrellas y un Lucero, composed by Aniel's uncle René Casanova Lugo. On this album, Dagoberto is the living thread between that family composition and its re-version seven decades later.

s7.label: The Songs
s7.intro: ON THIS RECORD, YOU WILL FIND:
s7.track9note: Re-version — composed by René Casanova Lugo (Aniel's uncle) · Orquesta Aragón classic
s7.track10note: Re-version — composed by Enrique Jorrín, inventor of the cha-cha-chá (1951)
